summary: The exact candidate moves the shared correctness and performance helpers into the importable flydsl.testing package API, retains tests.test_common as an identity-preserving compatibility re-export, migrates repository consumers, and fixes the prior eager undeclared pandas dependency. The original base failure was reproduced, and the candidate passed its focused regression plus independent pandas-absent, compatibility, default-profiler, and real-GPU numerical checks.

tests.command: env PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-d5a1acae73b1/venv/bin/python -c 'import flydsl; from flydsl.testing import checkAllclose, run_perftest' (on base acf7e67b7d22847e345938ca54fcc137bd7b2a1f)
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction of the original requested public import; flydsl loaded from the prepared source tree and failed because flydsl.testing did not exist.

tests.command: env PYTHONPATH=/job/repo/python:/job/repo HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-d5a1acae73b1/venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_testing.py tests/unit/test_compile_hints.py tests/kernels/test_vec_add.py -q
tests.what_was_measured: Candidate regression, legacy compatibility, helper behavior, compile-hint compatibility, and FlyDSL vector-add GPU execution: 29 passed and 2 existing architecture/feature cases skipped.

Independent subprocess blocked every pandas import, imported and used checkAllclose, and used run_perftest on an MI355X. GPU addition matched an independently constructed NumPy reference with max_abs_error=0.0; pandas remained unloaded.
Independent default torch.profiler/pandas timing path on an MI355X, including exact NumPy-reference agreement and positive measured latency.
Whitespace/error check for the exact candidate diff.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI355X (reported capability 9.5/gfx950) executed both the candidate vector-add regressions and independent run_perftest checks. The independent NumPy references had max_abs_error=0.0 for both event and profiler timing paths.

native_rebuild_evidence: No C++, MLIR, LLVM, CMake, or native binding source changed between the recorded base and exact candidate, so rebuilding native code was not applicable. Candidate Python came from /job/repo/python/flydsl/testing.py; the native extension resolved through /job/repo/python/flydsl/_mlir to the pinned /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/flydsl/_mlir tree, including _mlirDialectsFly.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so.
remaining_limitations: Only the assigned AMD Instinct MI355X/gfx950 architecture was available; CUDA/NVIDIA behavior and other AMD architectures were not exercised.
HIP graph mode was not independently exercised.
Two compile-hint cases were skipped by their existing architecture/feature guards.

The upstream ROCm/FlyDSL issue could not be queried live because the organization rejected the installed fine-grained token; review used the supplied original issue snapshot and accessible mirror records.
No release wheel was rebuilt because the candidate contains no native changes; package discovery was inspected and source-tree imports were verified against the exact candidate.
